t.5.8.1: Looking about there, Hanumān saw a splendid couch, heavenly in appearance, made of crystal and adorned with jewels.
t.5.8.2: And in one part of it he saw a white parasol adorned with the finest garlands, resembling the lord of the stars.
t.5.8.3: It was being fanned on every side by women holding yak-tail whisks in their hands, suffused with fragrances of many kinds, and perfumed with the finest incense.
t.5.8.4: He beheld it spread with the finest coverings, overlaid with sheepskins, and adorned on every side with strands of choice garlands.
t.5.8.5: On it he beheld one who resembled a dark rain-cloud, wearing blazing, splendid earrings, red-eyed and mighty-armed, and clad in garments of gold.
t.5.8.6: He saw him, his limbs anointed with fragrant red sandal paste, like a cloud in the sky reddened by twilight and laced with a streak of lightning.
t.5.8.7: Adorned with divine ornaments, handsome, able to take any form at will, he lay like Mount Mandara asleep, rich with its trees, woods and thickets.
t.5.8.8: He lay at rest after his sport in the night, adorned with excellent ornaments, beloved of the rākṣasa maidens and a bringer of happiness to the rākṣasas.
t.5.8.9: That great monkey saw the heroic lord of the rākṣasas who, having drunk, had come to rest and lay fast asleep on a radiant couch.
t.5.8.10: Having come upon Rāvaṇa, who was breathing heavily like a serpent, that best of monkeys, deeply agitated, drew back as if greatly frightened.
t.5.8.11: Then, having reached the ascent and taking his place within the platform, the great monkey beheld the tiger among rākṣasas lying asleep.
t.5.8.12: The excellent couch of the lord of the Rākṣasas, as he lay sleeping, shone forth like a great mountain cascade when a mighty musth elephant has lain down beside it.
t.5.8.13: And he saw the two arms of the great-souled lord of the rākṣasas, bound with golden armlets, flung out and resembling the banners of Indra.
t.5.8.14: He saw those two arms, scarred with wounds inflicted by the pressing tips of Airāvata's tusks, their stout shoulders scored by the thunderbolt, and gashed by the discus of Viṣṇu.
t.5.8.15: Those two arms were stout, with even and well-formed shoulders, firmly knit and endowed with strength; their nails and thumbs bore auspicious marks, and they were distinguished by fine fingers and palms.
t.5.8.16: His two arms, compact and massive like iron bars, rounded and resembling the trunks of elephants, lay flung out upon the gleaming white bed like a pair of five-headed serpents.
t.5.8.17: His two arms were well anointed with costly sandal paste, very cool and fragrant, the color of a hare's blood, and they were beautifully adorned.
t.5.8.19: That monkey saw his two arms resting upon the couch, like two great angry serpents asleep within a cave of Mandara.
t.5.8.18: Those two arms, caressed by the finest women and anointed with the most excellent perfumes, had made Yakṣas, Pannagas, Gandharvas, Devas and Dānavas cry out.
t.5.8.20: With those two full, well-rounded arms, the lord of the Rākṣasas, resembling a mountain, shone like Mandara with its two peaks.
t.5.8.22: From the mouth of that lion among rākṣasas, as he lay sleeping, there issued a mighty breath, as though filling that house.
t.5.8.21: It was sweet with the scent of mango and puṃnāga blossoms, mingled with the finest bakula, blended with the savour of well-prepared food, and led by the aroma of drinks.
t.5.8.23: His face glowed with earrings and was set off by a radiant golden crown, studded with pearls and gems, that had slipped aside.
t.5.8.24: It shone resplendent with a gleaming necklace smeared with red sandalwood paste, and likewise with a chest that was full, long and broad.
t.5.8.25: The one with blood-red eyes was well wrapped in a white linen cloth that had slipped loose, and in a costly yellow garment of the finest kind.
t.5.8.26: He looked like a heap of black beans, hissing as he breathed like a serpent, like an elephant fast asleep at the edge of the waters of the great Gaṅgā.
t.5.8.27: Him, his whole body lit up on all four sides by four blazing golden lamps, like a cloud illumined by hosts of lightning flashes.
t.5.8.28: And in the house of that most mighty lord of the rākṣasas, who loved his wives, he also saw his wives, who had gone to rest at his feet.
t.5.8.29: The leader of the monkey troops saw women whose faces shone like the moon, adorned with fine earrings, wearing unfaded garlands and ornaments.
t.5.8.30: The monkey saw them seated there, wearing excellent ornaments, women skilled in dance and instrumental music who had lain in the arms and on the lap of the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.5.8.31: On the edges of the women's ears he saw golden earrings set with diamonds and cat's-eye gems, and armlets as well.
t.5.8.33: Those slender-waisted wives of the lord of the Rākṣasas, wearied by intoxication and exertion, lay fast asleep here and there in various places.
t.5.8.32: With their lovely moon-like faces, graced with swaying earrings, that aerial palace shone like the sky with its hosts of stars.
t.5.8.34: One woman, asleep with her vīṇā clasped in her arms, shone like a lotus plant swept along by a great river and clinging to a boat.
t.5.8.35: Another lovely dark-eyed woman, asleep with a maḍḍuka drum resting in the crook of her arm, looked like a tender mother holding her little son.
t.5.8.36: A woman lovely in every limb, with beautiful breasts, lay asleep pressing a drum to herself, like a passionate woman embracing her lover after obtaining him at long last.
t.5.8.38: Another woman, her eyes heavy with intoxication, lay fast asleep, pressing a mṛdaṅga drum against her soft, full, and charming limbs that gleamed like gold.
t.5.8.37: One lotus-eyed woman lay asleep embracing a shoulder; overcome by slumber, that passionate lady seemed like a beloved woman resting together with her lover.
t.5.8.39: A slender-waisted, faultless woman lay asleep with a paṇava drum held in her armpit, resting in the space between her arm and her side, weary from the exhaustion of intoxication.
t.5.8.40: Another lovely woman, having taken hold of a ḍiṇḍima drum, lay fast asleep with the drum clinging to her, as though she were embracing a young calf.
t.5.8.42: Another lovely woman, who had cast aside her water-jar and fallen asleep, shone like a garland in springtime, variegated with flowers and freshly sprinkled clean.
t.5.8.41: One lotus-petal-eyed woman lay fast asleep, overcome by intoxication, having clasped an āḍambara drum, pressing it in the embrace of her arms.
t.5.8.43: And another woman, overcome by the power of sleep, lay sleeping, clasping with both hands her breasts, which were like golden pitchers.
t.5.8.44: Another, lotus-petal-eyed, with a face like the full moon, a lady of shapely hips, lay fast asleep embracing another woman, overcome with intoxication.
t.5.8.45: Excellent women lay asleep embracing their beautiful musical instruments and pressing them to their breasts, like amorous women clasping their lovers.
t.5.8.46: Apart from those women, the monkey saw another woman, endowed with beauty, lying on a splendid couch placed in a secluded spot.
t.5.8.47: She was splendidly adorned with ornaments set with pearls and gems, and seemed, as it were, to adorn that finest of mansions with her own radiance.
t.5.8.48: There the monkey saw Mandodarī lying asleep: fair-skinned, shining with the hue of gold, the beloved mistress of the inner apartments, lovely in form.
t.5.8.50: He slapped his arms, kissed his tail, rejoiced, frolicked, sang and ran about; he climbed the pillars and dropped down to the ground, displaying the very nature of monkeys.
t.5.8.49: Seeing her so adorned, the mighty-armed son of the Wind guessed from her wealth of beauty and youth that she was Sītā, and the leader of the monkey troops, filled with great joy, rejoiced.
